ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, within $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=4$, $BC=3$. Let point P be a moving point on the hypotenuse $AB$. Draw $PE\perp AC$ at point E and $PF\perp BC$ at point F. Connect $EF$. Then, the minimum value of the line segment $EF$ is
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $PC$,\\
since $PE\perp AC$ and $PF\perp BC$,\\
therefore $\angle PEC = \angle PFC = 90^\circ$,\\
thus quadrilateral $ECFP$ is a rectangle,\\
hence $EF=PC$,\\
thus, when $PC$ is at its minimum, $EF$ is also at its minimum,\\
which is when $CP\perp AB$, $PC$ is at its minimum,\\
since $AC=4$ and $BC=3$,\\
therefore $AB=5$,\\
thus, the minimum value of $PC$ is: $ \frac{AC\cdot BC}{AB}=\frac{4\times 3}{5}=\boxed{2.4}$\\
therefore, the minimum length of segment $EF$ is 2.4.

Draw $PE\perp AC$ at point $E$ and $PF\perp BC$ at point $F$. Connect $EF$. Then, the minimum value of the line segment $EF$ is
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Draw $PC$. Since $PE\perp AC$ and $PF\perp BC$, we have $\angle PEC=\angle PFC=90^\circ$, so quadrilateral $ECFP$ is a rectangle. Hence $EF=PC$. Therefore, minimizing $EF$ is equivalent to minimizing $PC$, which occurs when $CP\perp AB$. Given $AC=4$, $BC=3$, so $AB=5$. Thus the minimum value is $PC_{\min}=\frac{AC\cdot BC}{AB}=\frac{4\times 3}{5}=2.4$. Therefore, the minimum length of $EF$ is $2.4$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is right triangle ABC, there is a right-angle mark at vertex C, AB is the base, and P is located on AB. Point E is on AC, and in the figure PE is perpendicular to AC; point F is on BC, and in the figure PF is perpendicular to BC; segment EF has been connected. Then reason: Because AC ⟂ BC, and PE ⟂ AC, therefore PE ∥ BC; also because PF ⟂ BC, therefore PF ∥ AC. Therefore the two pairs of opposite sides of quadrilateral ECFP are respectively parallel, and there is a right angle, so ECFP is a rectangle. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, therefore EF = CP. To find the minimum value of EF is equivalent to finding the minimum value of CP when P moves on AB. The shortest distance from a point to a line is the perpendicular segment, so when CP ⟂ AB, CP is minimum. From AC = 4, BC = 3, and ∠C = 90°, it can be obtained that AB = √(4² + 3²) = 5. In a right triangle, the altitude from C to hypotenuse AB is AC·BC/AB = 4×3/5 = 12/5 = 2.4. Therefore the minimum value of EF is 2.4.
